Reddit spent years as the internet’s best-kept secret. In 2026, the secret’s out. It’s one of the web’s fastest-growing platforms and a primary source powering AI search results. The conversations happening inside its communities shape what your customers read everywhere else.


That shift changes the math for marketers. Use these current Reddit statistics to benchmark your audience, understand user behavior and refine your[Reddit marketing](https://sproutsocial.com/insights/marketing-on-reddit/) strategy.


Here’s what the latest data makes clear:


-


Reddit crossed[514.6 million weekly active uniques](https://resourcera.com/data/social/reddit-statistics/) for the first time in Q2 2026, with daily active uniques up 18% year over year. Its audience is scaling fast, so early movers still have room to build authority.


-


The US is Reddit’s largest single market at 194.8 million users and 42.95% of traffic, but international daily users now outpace it. Your reach here isn’t capped by borders.


-


Only[22% of social users have a Reddit profile](https://sproutsocial.com/insights/data/2026-social-media-content-strategy-report/) , yet the platform’s influence runs far deeper than that number suggests. Lurkers and searchers, not just registered accounts, drive its reach.


## Reddit user demographics statistics


-


[48% of US adults](https://www.statista.com/statistics/261766/share-of-us-internet-users-who-use-reddit-by-age-group/) who use Reddit are between 18–29 years old, followed by 30–49-year-olds.


-


As of 2026, 59.8% of[users identified as male](https://www.statista.com/statistics/1255182/distribution-of-users-on-reddit-worldwide-gender/) and 39.7% as female.


-


In 2025, US[users’ ethnicities](https://www.statista.com/statistics/261770/share-of-us-internet-users-who-use-reddit-by-ethnicity/) were 27% White, 18% Black, 22% Hispanic and 44% Asian.


-


[Reddit’s largest audiences outside the US](https://worldpopulationreview.com/country-rankings/reddit-users-by-country) are in the UK (45.8 million), Canada (43.1 million), India (30.8 million), Germany (29.3 million) and Australia (23.3 million).


-


International daily users (77.1 million) now[outpace US daily users (53.2 million)](https://investor.redditinc.com/news-events/news-releases/news-details/2026/Reddit-Reports-Second-Quarter-2026-Results/default.aspx) and are growing around 28% a year.


Reddit’s users lean young, making it a valuable social media platform for reaching Gen Z and younger millennials. While it reaches US audiences well, India, the United Kingdom and Canada also have notable bases.


These data points reveal a unique advantage for brands targeting[social media demographics](https://sproutsocial.com/insights/new-social-media-demographics/) like Reddit’s through authenticity, community engagement and value-first organic interactions.


Targeting niche subreddits lets you focus on high-intent topics. Localized subreddits also allow teams to tailor campaigns by city or country.


Use these demographic insights to build a targeted[Reddit marketing strategy](https://sproutsocial.com/insights/reddit-marketing-strategy/) that connects with high-intent audiences.


## How Reddit users engage: Understanding behavior and traffic


On Reddit.com, you can increase engagement in a few ways. People spot your post or comment in their feed, or find you inside a specific subreddit. The other big driver is search engines.


Reddit is a popular place for real information. Because of Google’s[$60 million yearly deal with Reddit](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/google-reddit-60-million-deal-ai-training/) and how people search, many internet users find Reddit posts through search engines.


Here are the key Reddit traffic and behavior numbers driving that discovery:


-


As of Q2 2026, Reddit reached over[130 million active daily users](https://www.statista.com/statistics/1453133/reddit-quarterly-dau-by-online-status/?srsltid=AfmBOooJLoI6V9Df8VacN_mVLAhafCjHAJSlKwp2TQINiSpLTNmibnJG) —77.7 million logged out and 52.6 million logged in.


-


That means 59.7% of daily users browse Reddit while logged out.


-


Organic search sends roughly[66.88% of Reddit’s traffic](https://foundationinc.co/lab/reddit-statistics/) , which is exactly why that Google deal matters.


-


More than[80 million people search directly on Reddit](https://searchengineland.com/reddit-search-80-million-people-468598) each week.


-


Reddit has[2.3 billion backlinks from 1.4 million referring domains](https://foundationinc.co/lab/reddit-statistics/) .


[Foundation Marketing’s analysis of Reddit stats](https://foundationinc.co/lab/reddit-statistics/) reveals key post performance benchmarks:


-


Titles between 160–180 characters earned the most upvotes.


-


The performance gap between question and non-question titles is now statistically negligible, under 1%.


-


Longer, descriptive titles consistently outperform very short ones.


### Reddit user behavior & community norms


-


**Redditors engage with authenticity:** Reddit user behavior is often different from users on other social media platforms. They are invested in in-depth discussions about other people’s genuine thoughts, opinions and perspectives. Because of this, they’re invested in authentic discussions and are skeptical of promotional language and overt marketing.


-


**All users are expected to respect subreddit rules and guidelines:** Each subreddit has its own rules, guidelines and styles of engagement that all users are expected to follow. If you break those standards, you could easily lose trust, especially as a marketer. As a marketer, it’s important to understand community nuances and learn how users talk and think in the niche communities you’re involved in.


-


**Users trust the authenticity of product reviews on Reddit:** Since Reddit is a community-based platform, what users organically say about a product or business carries weight. To engage with redditors successfully, brands must join conversations and add enriching perspectives. And to maintain credibility across subreddits, avoid direct promotional pitches.


-


**Redditors especially engage in the comments:** The real value for users lies in the comment section of posts. Users have countless conversations that rabbit trail from the original post’s initial discussion. Your brand can hop into the myriad of conversations within just one thread and build relational equity within that community.


Mastering these community norms positions your brand to build genuine traction across subreddits.


But it’s worth noting that Reddit growth takes diligence, time and patience.


Consistent Reddit engagement on a healthy cadence matters. If you want to convert your traffic and increase your subreddit following, stay genuinely engaged in conversations where you can show your expertise and offer helpful perspectives. Be sure to foster connections in subreddit communities by following different redditors you engage with in meaningful discussions.


One way to nurture your audience is by hosting an AMA (Ask Me Anything). It adds a lot of value and builds your credibility. For example, if you’re a social media manager for a coffee shop, you could host an AMA on a local subreddit that encourages users to ask about your company’s methods to produce high-quality coffee or how you manage solid profit margins through different seasons.


## Reddit revenue and growth statistics


Reddit isn’t just growing its audience, it’s proving it can monetize one. That financial momentum tells you the ad platform is maturing fast, and worth a budget test.


-


Reddit’s revenue reached[$2.2 billion in 2025](https://investor.redditinc.com/news-events/news-releases/news-details/2026/Reddit-Reports-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Year-2025-Results-Announces-1-Billion-Share-Repurchase-Program/default.aspx) , a 69% jump year over year.


-


The company posted net income of $530 million in fiscal 2025, a swing from a $484 million loss the year before.


-


Advertising revenue hit[$762 million in Q2 2026](https://investor.redditinc.com/news-events/news-releases/news-details/2026/Reddit-Reports-Second-Quarter-2026-Results/default.aspx) , up 64% year over year.


-


Reddit’s valuation climbed to[roughly $30 billion in 2026](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/RDDT/key-statistics/) .


Reddit’s monetization is scaling without slowing audience growth. For brands, that’s your cue to test the platform now while ad costs and competition are still climbing.

## Leveraging niche subreddits and how they shape trends


Many[subreddits shape social trends](https://sproutsocial.com/insights/reddit-trends/) by sparking viral posts that users share on different platforms. Some are so influential that they’ve even inspired movies and documentaries, like r/wallstreetbets[influencing the GameStop stock surge](https://sproutsocial.com/insights/gamestop-stock-social-media/) , leading Wall Street to intervene. Your brand can leverage the power of community by posting on these top subreddits or targeted subreddits where your audience is.


Posting to niche communities can also offer great potential. Let’s say you own a restaurant that serves Mexican food in Toronto with a college-age customer base. You can explore subreddits like:


-


**r/Ontario:** 973k members


-


**r/Toronto:** 827k members


-


**r/FoodToronto:** 71k members


-


**r/UofT (University of Toronto):** 126k members


Targeting specific communities like r/FoodToronto and r/UofT is a smart way to reach your ideal customer.


In 2025,[Reddit announced that it’s considering paywalls](https://www.businessinsider.com/reddit-ceo-says-paid-subreddits-coming-platfor-soon-2025-2) for specific subreddits. This change can generate new opportunities for paid communities that provide access to more qualified, topic-specific audiences.


-


Find brand-specific questions and answer them.


-


Post about new features or services in places like r/AMA or host an AMA on a niche subreddit.


-


Grow your Karma (Reddit’s point system) by providing in-depth answers in key subreddits.


-


Announce discounts, contests and event information in relevant subreddits.


-


Respond to pressing news to create buzz among your most passionate target audience.


## Reddit advertising and brand engagement statistics


As Reddit grows and companies like Google invest, marketers have even more reasons to dive into the community-driven platform. Consider these stats:


1.


[Users are 46% more likely to trust brands](https://www.business.reddit.com/advertise) with ads on Reddit. Consumers reached through Reddit have a 1.7x higher brand association, and brands enjoy a 12% increase in brand favorability among customers.


2.


Companies have seen promising results from Reddit Ads, like[Liquid I.V., which achieved a 94% reduction](https://www.business.reddit.com/success-stories/liquid-i-v-q223) in cost per action and 17x return on ads.


Reddit users don’t just tolerate brands, they reward the ones that show up with substance. Our 2026 Social Media Content Strategy Report found that 54% of users engage with user-generated content on Reddit, and customer service (21%) is the top reason people want brands there in the first place.


[Ramp](https://www.reddit.com/r/Ramp/) puts this into practice, running its own subreddit for customer service and hosting executive AMAs that turn support questions into public proof of expertise.


To maximize your Reddit Ad strategy, apply these key tactics:


-


**Place laser-targeted ads:** Use Reddit Ads to place advertisements in niche, relevant subreddits. You’ll get direct access to a specific audience.


-


**Use Reddit formats:** Incorporate formats like Conversation Ads and Carousel Ads for more interactive, native experiences. For example, a Carousel Ad can show product benefits in a visual format.


-


**Leverage data:** Build, learn and iterate your ads with[Reddit data](https://sproutsocial.com/insights/reddit-analytics-tools/) . Set aside a budget for A/B test headlines, subreddits and creative formats.


-


**Engage with the ad:** When users leave comments on a Conversation Ad, keep the discussion going and engage with your audience. Use your conversations and findings to fuel ideas for future organic interactions with posts, AMAs and comments.


Combine organic community engagement with targeted[Reddit Ads](https://sproutsocial.com/insights/reddit-advertising/) to maximize reach, build trust and drive performance.


## How to use Reddit statistics to inform your social strategy


Reddit’s user base and niche communities offer valuable insights and opportunities to connect with your target audience. Tap into the social media platform and use these Reddit insights to:


-


**Leverage subreddit-level market insights:** You can leverage Reddit’s advanced search features and[Reddit social listening](https://sproutsocial.com/insights/reddit-social-listening/) to learn more about your ideal customers in the communities where they’re most active. Start by analyzing the most upvoted threads, user feelings in the comments, common questions and pain points.


-


**Drive brand visibility with community-powered content:** While engaging with posts is a major part of a healthy Reddit marketing strategy, find ways to invite collaboration. Think of tactics like posting polls, inviting user feedback on a project or product idea, hosting an AMA or announcing a giveaway. These community-involved approaches can boost engagement and trust for your brand. Center your strategies on education and transparency over in-your-face promotion.


-


**Track Reddit mentions and brand interactions:** Use a social listening tool to detect brand mentions and conversations. This insight allows you to enter discussions naturally and engage authentically. The right tool will use alerts for mentions that let you join conversations and shape how audiences view your brand.


When implementing these actions, always follow a subreddit’s rules and guidelines. Moderators manage many communities and ban obvious spam or promotional materials. An organic, community-driven approach will work best.


Because Reddit can be more anonymous, it’s an excellent platform for unfiltered feedback and thoughts. According to our 2026 Social Media Content Strategy Report, nearly one-third of all social users turn to Reddit to connect with niche communities, making it an essential space for social listening that can help you spot key opportunities.


Now that you understand the numbers behind Reddit’s growth, learn the step-by-step process of[how to use Reddit](https://sproutsocial.com/insights/how-to-use-reddit/) to connect with these engaged communities and achieve your marketing goals.

## FAQs about Reddit statistics


Are Reddit users increasing or decreasing?


Increasing—and fast. Reddit’s daily active users have posted double-digit year-over-year growth, according to[Resourcera](https://resourcera.com/data/social/reddit-statistics/) . The platform crossed 130 million daily actives in Q2 2026, with international growth outpacing the US and showing no signs of slowing down.


How much time does the average user spend on Reddit?


The average user spends about[10 minutes and 23 seconds per visit](https://www.businessofapps.com/data/reddit-statistics/) , often clicking through multiple threads in a single session.


What is the 90-9-1 rule on Reddit?


The 90-9-1 rule describes online participation: Roughly 90% of people lurk, 9% comment or engage occasionally and 1% create most of the content.
